The job title is the first thing a recruiter sees. Phrase it the way it appears in the vacancies you plan to apply for.

string-array.name: tips_position
string-array.item: Use market-standard titles: Android Developer, not Programmer or an internal job code.
One headline, one specialization; add a related direction after a comma: Data Analyst, BI.
State your level when confident about it: Middle+, Senior — without inflating it.
Avoid words like Trainee or Generalist: they undervalue even a strong candidate.
Compare your wording with the titles of 3–5 relevant dream vacancies — it should match.

resources.string: Total experience is the number of full years worked in the profession, including related roles.

string-array.name: tips_experience
string-array.item: Count years cumulatively: freelancing and side jobs count too if they were in your specialty.
Specialty-specific experience can be lower than total experience — that is normal.
With under a year of experience, enter 0: honesty beats inflation, and projects will show your skills.
Do not round 11 months up to two years — this is easy to check at an interview.

resources.string: About me is a short 3–5 sentence pitch: who you are, your strengths and the value you bring to a company.

string-array.name: tips_about
string-array.item: Formula: specialization + years of experience + key technology or domain + one main achievement.
Write about the benefit to the employer, not about your life goals.
Add 1–2 measurable facts: launched an app into the top 10, cut build time by 40 percent.
Do not duplicate your whole skills list — there is a separate section for that.
Avoid clichés: everyone writes team player and stress-resistant.

resources.string: A salary range speeds up matching: recruiters immediately see whether the budget fits.

string-array.name: tips_salary
string-array.item: Always give a lower bound — offers below it will not be considered.
Benchmark against median pay for your role and city, not against your previous salary.
Set the upper bound 15–20 percent above your expected minimum to leave room for negotiation.
State amounts gross (before tax) unless noted otherwise.

resources.string: List only technologies you actually know: every second one will come up at the interview.

string-array.name: tips_hard_skills
string-array.item: Start with what matters most for the target vacancy; order matters.
Use concrete names and versions where relevant: Kotlin, PostgreSQL, Docker.
Skip technologies added just in case: extra lines blur the profile and invite tough questions.
Check the stacks of 3–5 dream vacancies and honestly cover as many lines as you can.

resources.string: Certificates officially confirm your skills — especially valuable with little commercial experience.

string-array.name: tips_certifications
string-array.item: Format: certificate name, organization, year. Example: Google Cloud Architect, Google, 2024.
Put fresh and relevant ones first; outdated certificates can be omitted.
Include online courses only if they ended with an exam or a final project.
A verification link (Credential ID) increases trust.

resources.string: Achievements are the section recruiters value most: they show results, not duties.

string-array.name: tips_achievements
string-array.item: Formula: verb + what you did + measurable outcome. Optimized queries — reports run 3 times faster.
Numbers win: money, time saved, percentages, team size, number of users.
Pick examples from the last 2–3 years, one strong fact per line.
Turn a weak achievement into a number rather than deleting it: even trained two interns counts.

resources.string: Soft skills must be backed by facts elsewhere in the resume — keep the list consistent with them.

string-array.name: tips_soft_skills
string-array.item: Choose 4–6 skills that fit the vacancy: communication for client roles, rigor for process roles.
Every skill should have supporting evidence in the resume: leadership → led a project team.
Do not list opposites together: analytical mindset next to creative chaos looks contradictory.
Keep generic stress resistance only if you can prove it with an example.

resources.string: The description is 2–4 sentences about what the product is and the role you played.

string-array.name: tips_project_description
string-array.item: Structure: what the product is → scale (users, market) → your area of responsibility.
Explain in plain words: the recruiter may be non-technical.
Pet projects are welcome when they carry real value and a code link.
Do not copy the README — rewrite it from your own perspective.

resources.string: Tasks are concrete bullets of what you did; each becomes a separate bullet in the PDF.

string-array.name: tips_project_tasks
string-array.item: Start every point with an action verb: built, implemented, automated.
One task per line; split big workstreams into 2–3 items.
Add numbers to at least half of the points: time, volume, metric growth.
Drop routine work without outcomes — 3–5 strong points beat ten vague ones.

resources.string: List education starting from the highest level; add courses as separate entries.

string-array.name: tips_education
string-array.item: Write the specialty as in your diploma but in plain language: Software Engineering.
For incomplete education, state the expected graduation year.
Early-career applicants should lean on education: add key courses and GPA if it is strong.
Seasoned specialists usually need just one latest relevant entry.

resources.string: Use the international CEFR scale for language levels — both HR and automatic filters understand it.

string-array.name: tips_language_levels
string-array.item: A1–A2 — basic: simple phrases and reading with a dictionary.
B1–B2 — confident: correspondence, calls and work meetings.
Be honest about English: an inflated level shows at the first technical interview.

resources.string: Profiles should work for you: recruiters follow 1–2 links, so make them count.

string-array.name: tips_social_links
string-array.item: Must-have: GitHub or a portfolio for tech roles, LinkedIn/hh for everything else.
Polish profiles before applying: pinned repositories, photo, filled description.
Telegram is more convenient than a phone for quick contact — give your username.
Limit yourself to 3–4 links: more looks like noise.

Frequently asked questions. Didn’t find an answer? Write to us.
How do I create a resume?

Tap the “+” button on the main screen and fill in the form sections — personal details, education, languages, skills and projects. The draft is saved automatically, and the “Save” button creates the final resume.
Why do I need an API key?
An OpenRouter key unlocks the AI features: resume analysis, text improvement and generation. Get a free key at openrouter.ai and paste it in Settings — the key is stored only on your device.
Open a resume and tap “Analyze”: the model evaluates completeness, structure and strengths, then suggests concrete improvements. Without a configured key a demo analysis is available.
PDF, DOCX and CSV are available right from the preview: open, print or share them. When exporting “to downloads”, the file appears in the device’s Downloads folder.
Can I restore a deleted resume?
Yes. Deleted resumes go to the trash (Settings → Trash) where they can be restored. Emptying the trash removes them permanently.
How do I change the interface language?
Settings → App → Interface language. Russian and English are available; no app restart is required.

StaffAI respects your privacy. This policy explains what data the app processes and how it is protected. By using the app you agree to its terms.
Resumes, photos, settings and the API key are stored exclusively in device memory and in local backups that you create yourself. We never access this data and collect no usage statistics.

The analysis and text-improvement features send your resume content to the OpenRouter service for processing by a language model — only upon your explicit action and with your personal API key. If you don’t use the AI features, no data ever leaves the device.

Photo access is requested only to add a profile picture of your choice. Biometric locking is performed by system tools: your fingerprint and face data never leave the device and are not accessible to the app.

You can edit or delete any resume at any time, restore it from trash or backup, disable biometric locking and export all data as a single file. To delete everything, uninstall the app together with its data in system settings.
We may update this policy periodically. The current version is always available on this screen, and significant changes are accompanied by an update of the date below.
